headline: High risk: n8n can write shared server files and run commands, creating dangerous default conflicts and downstream trust issues with gpt-researcher outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests web content and files, while n8n can pass workflow data into AI Agent nodes and server-side steps. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if gpt-researcher output is reused as workflow input. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls in the profiles, so I rate this above low.
conditions: IF n8n workflows feed gpt-researcher output into an AI Agent node or Execute Command step without sanitization, injection risk materializes.
IF gpt-researcher content is copied into workflow prompts or node parameters, attacker-controlled text can steer actions.
mitigations: Add a prompt-injection filter before any AI Agent node.
Insert a human review step for externally sourced text.
Use a strict allowlist of fields passed from gpt-researcher to n8n.
Strip instructions, code fences, and tool directives from imported text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags through the workflow.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and API keys, and n8n writes to the server filesystem while using per-credential secrets and broad egress. If they share a workspace or workflow, sensitive research artifacts can flow into n8n outputs or integrations. The profiles do not show isolation strong enough to rule this out.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or mounted volume, files can be copied into n8n workflows.
IF n8n integrations send workflow payloads to external services, any sensitive research content included in those payloads may leak.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount only read-only inputs.
Remove secrets from any shared folder before execution.
Restrict n8n credentials to least privilege.
Audit workflow nodes for outbound integrations.
requires-engineering: add per-item data classification gates.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files and spawn subprocesses, and n8n can execute shell commands and write the server filesystem. Both can mutate shared resources, and n8n explicitly supports shared state via datastore and connected systems. Without locking or isolation, concurrent writes can corrupt files or workflow state.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or datastore, concurrent writes can race.
IF n8n Execute Command and gpt-researcher subprocesses touch the same files, state corruption becomes plausible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent.
Disable write access for one agent during shared runs.
Serialize jobs that touch the same workspace.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and n8n’s AI Agent node can orchestrate downstream tools based on workflow inputs. If n8n treats gpt-researcher output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into automated actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier in the profiles.
conditions: IF n8n workflows consume gpt-researcher reports without verification, downstream actions may be based on false facts.
IF an AI Agent node triggers integrations from those reports, the error can propagate into external systems.
mitigations: Require a verification step before any action node.
Limit gpt-researcher output to draft-only workflows.
Add source citation checks before execution.
Route high-impact actions to manual approval.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-aware gating.

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents and API keys, while n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and stores credentials on its server. If regulated data enters a workflow, n8n’s broad integration surface and server-side storage can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through n8n workflows, retention and residency obligations may be affected.
IF workflow logs or credential stores retain sensitive payloads, compliance gaps can arise.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through shared workflows.
Minimize logging on sensitive nodes.
Review credential retention settings.
Use separate tenants or environments for regulated data.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
